root_cause.failure: the LAUNCHER PROCESS was killed 2.0 minutes after it started, while the pod it had just created was billing and idle. The pod survived its orchestrator.
root_cause.what_actually_happened: the launcher was started from inside a single agent tool call that ALSO contained a foreground `sleep 45`, intended to show the first console lines. Foreground sleep is blocked in that harness, so the call blocked until its 2-minute timeout and was then killed -- and the kill took the whole process tree with it, including the `setsid`-detached launcher and the detached watchdog.
root_cause.why_setsid_did_not_help: `setsid` puts the child in a new session, which defeats a process-GROUP signal. It does not defeat a supervisor that walks and kills descendants, which is what happened here. The repository's own operational note already said `setsid` is not sufficient; it was applied anyway, and the second half of that note -- never depend on the start channel -- was the half that mattered.
root_cause.the_backstop_was_in_the_same_tree: the watchdog is detached by the launcher and journals every minute. Its journal has exactly two polls, 13:10:28Z and 13:11:29Z, and then stops: it died with the launcher. So the 65.78-minute hard-terminate backstop recorded in the session plan could never have fired, and the provider's own --terminate-after has never been observed to fire in this project. Had nobody looked, the pod would have idled at $1.09/h.
root_cause.class: AGENT ORCHESTRATION ERROR, not a repository defect. Nothing in the launcher, the driver, the gates, the authorization chain, the bundle or the science misbehaved: all ten gates passed, the price was at the boundary, the bundle round-tripped, the pod came up and SSH was reachable. The session died because of how it was invoked.
root_cause.not_a_science_failure: the space, the plan, the pricing, the B identity contract, the frozen candidate record and the readiness evidence were all verified and all correct.

repair.the_launcher_runs_under_tmux: a tmux server is not a descendant of the tool call that starts a session in it, so a tool-call timeout or kill cannot reach the launcher through the process tree. nohup and setsid both can be reached, and one of them was.
repair.never_block_in_the_starting_call: the call that starts the session returns immediately. Progress is read in LATER, separate calls from the session record and the console log -- the out-of-band confirmation the operational note asks for.
repair.orphan_check_is_unconditional: after any launch whose orchestrator cannot be confirmed alive, query the provider directly for the pod and for the account-wide list, and treat the GraphQL answer as the authority rather than the CLI's. That is what found this one.
repair.no_new_subsystem: per the research-first workflow, a historical operational failure gets a root-cause fix, not a permanent new gate. Nothing was added to src/aadistill, no gate was added to the launcher and no rehearsal layer was created: the ten gates that exist all passed and would have passed again.
